facts.label: Duas formas de passado
facts.sub: Use o passado simples para fatos: I swam for an hour. Use was/were + -ing para ações em andamento: I was floating when it got dark.

facts.label: Passado simples
facts.sub: Use o passado simples para fatos terminados: I swam for an hour. He blew the whistle. We left. Swim, blow e leave são irregulares: swam, blew, left.

facts.label: Passado contínuo
facts.sub: Use was/were + -ing para o que estava em andamento: I was floating. Many people were swimming. Use when para o momento curto: when the lights went out.

compare.br: No Brasil, contamos “Eu nadei” e “Eu estava boiando quando…”.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: The past of swim is swam.
The past of blow is blowed.
I was floating is past progressive.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: The past of swim is swam. → Verdadeiro (Yes, it is irregular.)
The past of blow is blowed. → Falso (It is blew.)
I was floating is past progressive. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: An indoor pool · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Friday evening at a big indoor pool in Toronto. The water is calm and blue. Ugo is a lifeguard and sits on a high chair. Bia climbs out of the water with a towel. A few people still swim in the lanes. Ugo smiles and asks about her swim.
“Hi, Bia! You look happy. How was the pool?” says Ugo. “It was great! I swam for an hour.” says Bia. “What were you doing when the lights went out?” says Ugo.
